sample_unit: UWF images read in randomized crossover multi-reader study (four ophthalmologists)

links.outcome: Clinician sensitivity and specificity with versus without AI assistance in crossover multi-reader study
links.effect: AI assistance increased clinician sensitivity with minimal loss of specificity (600 UWF images; four ophthalmologists).
links.quote: In a prospectively registered randomized crossover multi-reader study (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07651943; 600 UWF images; four ophthalmologists), AI assistance increased clinician sensitivity with minimal loss of specificity.

links.outcome: Processing success, inference time and workflow disruption during silent deployment on consecutive examinations
links.effect: 100% processing success rate, median inference time ~1.1 seconds per examination, no workflow disruption across 37,665 consecutive examinations.
links.quote: During retrospective and prospective silent deployment involving 37,665 consecutive examinations, UWF-FM achieved a 100% processing success rate, a median inference time of approximately 1.1 seconds per examination, and no workflow disruption.

links.outcome: Model performance across external datasets and imaging vendors (Optos to Zeiss)
links.effect: Performance gains maintained across external datasets (10,686 external images) and cross-vendor evaluation (Optos to Zeiss) without additional adaptation.
links.quote: Performance gains were maintained across external datasets, clinically relevant operating thresholds, and cross-vendor evaluation (Optos to Zeiss) without additional adaptation.

unlisted_practices: Self-supervised pretraining of modality-specific foundation model on unlabeled images

screen.reason: Evaluates a retinal foundation model via a randomized crossover multi-reader trial (AI assistance vs unassisted) and silent-mode prospective clinical deployment across 37,665 consecutive examinations.

primary.practice: silent deployment and AI-assisted clinician reading
